papers.title: Nilpotent Deformation Theory via Ultrasolid Algebra
papers.abstract: Deformation theory studies how varieties and other algebro-geometric objects vary in families. A central part of the subject is formal deformation theory, where one deforms over an Artinian base; such deformation problems are governed by Lie algebraic models. We pose the question of deforming varieties over nilpotent but not necessarily Artinian bases. These turn out to be classified by the same Lie algebraic models plus some topological structure. More precisely, we will consider partition Lie algebroids in the category of ultrasolid modules, a variation of the solid modules of Clausen and Scholze that give a well-behaved category akin to topological modules. To approach this result, we decompose deformation problems into n-nilpotent layers. Each of these layers is individually easier to understand, and is classified by simpler variants of partition Lie algebras.

papers.title: Hyperplane arrangements with non-formal Milnor fibers
papers.abstract: Each complex hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ gives rise to a Milnor fibration of its complement. Building on work of Zuber, we give a combinatorial sufficient condition for the Milnor fiber $F(\mathcal{A})$ to be non-$1$-formal, expressed in terms of the multinet structure on $\mathcal{A}$, and use it to produce an infinite family of monomial arrangements $\mathcal{A}(3k,3k,3)$ with non-formal Milnor fibers. We also review the relevant background on cohomology jump loci, formality, and the topology of Milnor fibers of arrangements.

papers.title: The real Betti realization of very effective Hermitian K-theory
papers.abstract: Real Betti realization is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category of motivic spectra to that of topological spectra, extending the functor that associates to a scheme over $\mathbb{R}$ the space of its real points. In this article, we identify the $\mathcal{E}_1$-ring structure on the real realization of $\mathsf{ko}$, the very effective cover of Hermitian K-theory $\mathsf{KO}$, by an explicit 2-local fracture square, as being equivalent to $\mathsf{L}(\mathbb{R})_{\geq 0}$, the connective L-theory spectrum of $\mathbb{R}$. Along the way, we also compute the real realization of other motivic ring spectra: motivic cohomology $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}/2$, the variant $\widetilde{\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$, $\mathsf{KO}$, the very effective cover $\mathsf{kgl}$ of algebraic K-theory $\mathsf{KGL}$.

papers.title: Non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery
papers.abstract: We give homotopy-theoretic proofs of the principal results of non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery. These include the Fundamental Theorem of Poincar\'e surgery, the Poincar\'e transversality exact sequence, and the construction of Poincar\'e handle structures. All results apply in dimensions~$\ge 8$.

papers.title: Unbounded Nilpotency Gaps on Rationally Elliptic Manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct simply connected, closed smooth manifolds whose rational homotopy types are elliptic and whose homology nilpotency exceeds rational category by arbitrarily large amounts. This separates short models from short quotients of minimal models. The construction starts from an explicit family of minimal Sullivan algebras with finite-dimensional cohomology. A finite quotient establishes Poincar\'e duality and gives an upper bound for homology nilpotency, while a closed orientation functional computes rational category. Two forced primitives yield the lower bound. An even regrading separates the relevant weights, extending this obstruction to every graded acyclic differential ideal. Rational surgery realizes the resulting models in their formal dimensions, with vanishing rational Pontryagin classes and arbitrarily large rational connectivity. The ratio of homology nilpotency to rational category tends to four thirds. Finally, under an external spherical stabilization statement, attaching a single cone can increase homology nilpotency by an arbitrarily large amount while leaving rational category unchanged.

papers.title: Equivariant $K$-theory as a global localization
papers.abstract: We establish a global equivariant refinement of the theorem of Snaith that presents the complex $K$-theory spectrum as a localization of the suspension spectrum of $\mathbb C P^\infty$. We prove that the morphism of ultra-commutative global ring spectra from $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$ that classifies the tautological $U(1)$-representation exhibits the global $K$-theory spectrum as a specific localization, in both the $\infty$-categories of ultra-commutative ring spectra and of commutative global ring spectra. The classes to be inverted are certain representation-graded $U(n)$-equivariant homotopy classes of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$, the pre-Bott classes. We also show that for every compact Lie group $G$, the $G$-equivariant $K$-theory spectrum is a telescopic localization of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_G U(1)$ by the pre-Bott classes of all unitary $G$-representations.

papers.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.

papers.title: Normed idempotence of spectra and distributivity in equivariant higher algebra
papers.abstract: We introduce and develop the theory of distributivity for base categories equipped with so-called atomic orbital subcategories, with an eye towards applications in equivariant homotopy theory. This extends the important framework in Nardin's thesis and supplies several crucial details on distributivity missing from the treatment therein. As our main technical result, we provide a parametrised distributive version of the universal property of "partial cocompletions with relations". We then employ this to construct a distributively normed symmetric monoidal structure on presentable categories. In turn, by specialising to the case of equivariant homotopy theory for compact Lie groups G, we show that the category of genuine G-spectra is normed idempotent, so that we obtain the structure of multiplicative norms on G-spectra along inclusions of finite index subgroups.

papers.title: Integral homology lattices of matching and circulant complexes
papers.abstract: Bouc's hook cycles span the rational top homology of the matching complex of $K_{2k+1}$. We prove that their integral saturation quotient has exponent exactly $2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$ for every $k\geq1$, and construct divided-power cycles attaining this bound. For $k\geq2$, the homology lattice is not isomorphic to the standard integral hook lattice as an $\mathfrak S_{2k+1}$-module. For circulant complexes, we determine the integral dihedral homology modules of $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s}^{s-1})$, $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+1}^{s-1})$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+2}^{s-1})$, for $s\geq3$, $s\geq2$ and $s\geq3$, respectively, and classify the least scalar lifts of all primitive equivariant quotients to the rank-one module with trivial rotation and negative reflection. Tate localization relates prime-order gluing to fixed-point homology under a free, single-degree homology hypothesis. Explicit cycle subgroups separate saturation defects from obstructions to equivariant sections. For circulant independence complexes with jumps two and three, we prove an eight-periodic ordinary homotopy classification and a fixed-space obstruction to uniform representation suspensions. For every fixed nonempty bounded positive jump set, a finite-state construction gives a rational critical-face series.

papers.title: Global transfer systems and endopurity of subgroups
papers.abstract: Global transfer systems are combinatorial objects that parametrize intermediate levels of structures and properties in globally equivariant homotopy theory. In this paper we study the lattice of global transfer systems, expanding beyond the case of abelian groups which was computed by the second author. The main result is a proof that the irreducible elements of the lattice of global transfer systems are strictly controlled by subgroups of groups which we refer to as endopure. From the irreducible elements one can recover the whole lattice, and studying these endopure subgroups leads us to a wide range of new phenomena and computations.

papers.title: The invariant cell number property for $\mathbb{E}_4$-rings
papers.abstract: For any non-zero $\mathbb{E}_4$-ring $R$, we prove that an $n$-fold direct sum of suspensions of $R$ cannot admit an exhaustive filtration by fewer than $n$ cells. We do this by showing that certain integral representations of the symmetric group lift to Schur functors on additively $\mathbb{E}_3$-monoidal $\infty$-categories. We then reduce the statement to a vanishing fact for rational Schur functors due to Deligne.

papers.title: Resolutions of orbifold generalised triangle groups
papers.abstract: Let $T=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}=1\rangle$ be a generalised triangle group in which $W$ is the Farey word of a rational slope $q=r/s$, and suppose that $T$ is the fundamental group of a hyperbolic $3$-orbifold whose singular locus has no spherical vertices. Let $G=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}\rangle$ be the associated central extension. We compute an explicit free resolution of the trivial module over $\mathbb{Z}G$ of minimal length, with differentials given in closed form by Fox derivatives. From this resolution we deduce an explicit free resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ which is $2$-periodic in degrees at least two, and we compute the integral homology and cohomology of both groups. Strebel treated the classical family $q=0/1$ in 1983. Since then only the family $q=1/2$ has been treated, by Ellis and Williams, and for that family our resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ has strictly smaller rank in every degree.

papers.title: A counterexample to a conjecture of Plotnick on knot exteriors
papers.abstract: We resolve a conjecture of S. Plotnick from 1983 concerning the homotopy type of four-dimensional knot complements. We show that the exteriors of two branched twist spins of the trefoil, which were shown by Plotnick not to be homotopy equivalent as boundary pairs and hence not homeomorphic, are in fact simple homotopy equivalent. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of an explicit element of augmentation $49$ in the integral group ring of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ which is a unit modulo the group norm and commutes with the element inducing the monodromy on the fundamental group.

papers.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.

papers.title: The spectrum of units of algebraic $K$-theory
papers.abstract: It is well known that the $[0,1]$ and $[0,2]$ Postnikov truncations of the units of the topological $K$-theories $\glone \KO$ and $\glone \KU$, respectively, are split, and that the splitting is provided by the ($\Z/2$-graded) line bundles. In this paper we give a similar splitting for the $[0,1]$-truncation of the units of algebraic $K$-theory, considered as a sheaf on affine schemes. A crucial step is to produce the splitting for $\glone K(\Z)$. Along the way we also give a complete calculation of the connective spectrum of strict units of $K(\Z)$ and $K(\F_\ell)$ for a prime $\ell$. Finally, we show that the units of algebraic $K$-theory do not split as a presheaf. In fact we show they do not even split pointwise.

papers.title: Bar cohomology of links: beyond Milnor invariants
papers.abstract: We develop bar cohomology of link complements as an invariant of links in homology spheres. In this setting, bar cohomology is a Hopf algebra which is calculable using surfaces and their intersection curves in a link complement. In this first in a sequence of works, we introduce the invariant and show that it defines a canonical subspace of the tensor Hopf algebra, which already encodes information about Milnor's link invariants and provides geometrically significant information beyond them.

papers.title: On the fundamental groups of subelliptic varieties
papers.abstract: We show that the fundamental group of any smooth subelliptic variety is finite. Moreover, it is also proved that every finite group can be realized as the fundamental group of a smooth subelliptic variety. As a consequence, it follows that there exists a smooth subelliptic variety homotopy equivalent to the $n$-sphere if and only if $n>1$. This result can be considered as a negative answer to the algebraic version of Gromov's problem on the homotopy types of Oka manifolds.

papers.title: Topological Hochschild homology of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra II
papers.abstract: We compute topological Hochschild homology of $\mathbb{E}_3$-MU-algebra forms of the second truncated Brown-Peterson spectrum with Adams summand coefficients at $p=2$ and conditionally at arbitrary primes. We also provide a new computational tool, a variant of the Brun spectral sequence, for computing topological Hochschild homology of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra with certain coefficients. As a consequence, we show that $\mathbb{E}_3$-MU-algebra forms of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle$ are not Thom spectra at the prime $p=2$ for any $n\ge 2$.

papers.title: The chain replacement of a poset flow
papers.abstract: We introduce the chain replacement of a poset flow: it is obtained by considering the simplicial nerves of the posets of strictly increasing chains in the given poset, ordered by refinement. It maps posets to q-cofibrant flows and inclusions of posets to q-cofibrations. Using the combinatorial properties of the chain replacement, we prove that pushouts along the chain replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets induce trivial h-cofibrations on spaces of execution paths between states of the original flow. By introducing the Hurewicz model structure on flows (or H-model structure), we deduce the same property for any q-cofibrant replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets.

papers.title: Left properness of Moore flows
papers.abstract: We introduce reparametrization categories with cuts. For every such category $\mathcal{P}$, the tensor product of two objectwise weak homotopy equivalences of $\mathcal{P}$-spaces is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence, and the q-model structure on $\mathcal{P}$-flows is left proper. The reparametrization categories $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{M}$, as well as the terminal category $\mathbf{1}$, have cuts. The terminal category recovers the left properness of the q-model structure on ordinary flows. We also give a symmetric reparametrization category with cuts and a strict unit. This category is not equivalent to $\mathbf{1}$.

papers.title: Saturated directed spaces and generalized clocks
papers.abstract: We construct a Hausdorff saturated directed space whose directed path space between two distinct points has nontrivial fundamental group although the corresponding trace space is a square. A clock is a directed space with submetrizable underlying space; a timed space is a saturated directed space equipped with a regular directed map to a clock. Over every fixed clock, timed spaces form a locally presentable category, and their quotients from paths to traces are trivial Hurewicz fibrations with continuous sections. For Hausdorff saturated directed spaces whose compact subspaces are metrizable, these quotients are trivial q-fibrations. We construct a globular clock containing the directed circle and admitting regular maps from all q-cofibrant globular realizations, whereas a finite cellular example admits no regular map to the circle. Normalization also gives a proof of the quotient theorem for execution paths and establishes the homotopy lifting property for nondecreasing reparametrizations.
